cards.explanation: The answer is captain of the guard. Genesis 39:1 says it plainly: Potiphar is an officer of Pharaoh, Egypt's king, and captain of the guard. So Joseph lands in the house of a man with real rank. I got bought for 25 cents, friends, so a title like that makes me stand up a little straighter on my gold base.

The answer is the LORD. "And the LORD was with Joseph, and he became a successful man…" (Genesis 39:2). Joseph is far from home and serving in a stranger's house, but the text says the LORD is with him. Hold on to that line, friends, because it keeps showing up in this chapter. This is the heart of the whole story.

The answer is False. The text says Potiphar saw it. Verse 3 reads, "When his master saw that the LORD was with him and made him prosper in all he did…" Potiphar saw both who was with Joseph and how things went for him. That's what leads to Joseph finding favor in his sight.

The answer is household. Verse 4 says, "Potiphar put him in charge of his household and entrusted him with everything he owned." His household, friends. Joseph went from serving in the house to running it.

The answer is blesses. "…the LORD blessed the Egyptian's household on account of him." (Genesis 39:5). Blessing is the word the text uses. And it didn't stop at the front door, because "The LORD's blessing was on everything he owned, both in his house and in his field." All of that on account of Joseph.

The answer is False. Genesis 39:5 says, "The LORD's blessing was on everything he owned, both in his house and in his field." So it reaches the house and the field both. Nothing Potiphar owned was left out.

The answer is the food he eats. Verse 6 says Potiphar "did not concern himself with anything except the food he ate." Joseph had all he owned in his care, and the only thing left on Potiphar's mind was his meal. Friends, if the only thing on my mind were cookies, I'd need a bigger apron.

The answer is nothing except his wife. Joseph says, "He has withheld nothing from me except you, because you are his wife." (Genesis 39:9). He lays out how much Potiphar trusts him, and then he says that one line is the exception. The whole answer rests on that.

The answer is True. Joseph tells her, "No one in this house is greater than I am." (Genesis 39:9). He's pointing out how much Potiphar has trusted him with. Then he says what Potiphar held back: "…except you, because you are his wife."

The answer is a great evil and a sin against God. Joseph asks, "So how could I do such a great evil and sin against God?" (Genesis 39:9). Notice he names God in his answer. He calls it a great evil, and he calls it a sin against God. It's a clear no.

The answer is False. The text says more than the no. Genesis 39:10 says he "refused to go to bed with her or even be near her." She kept speaking to him day after day. He kept refusing, and he kept away from her.

The answer is that he leaves the cloak and runs outside. "But leaving his cloak in her hand, he escaped and ran outside." (Genesis 39:12). He didn't stop to grab it. He got out of that house. I've left things behind in a hurry, friends, but never anything that mattered this much.

The answer is that Joseph came to her and she screamed. She tells the servants, "He came to me so he could sleep with me, but I screamed as loud as I could." (Genesis 39:14). That is what she says, and it isn't what verse 12 says happened. I think this is a hard part of the story, friends.
The answer is True. She does mention the cloak. Verse 15 has her say, "…he left his cloak beside me and ran out of the house." The cloak shows up in her version, but it's her version.
The answer is False. Genesis 39:17 says, "Then she told him the same story…" She doesn't switch versions. Servants and husband both get the same account.
The answer is anger. Verse 19 says, "he burned with anger." That's the word the text uses for Potiphar. It doesn't say who the anger is aimed at, so I'll leave that open too.

The answer is that he has Joseph thrown into the king's prison. Verse 20 says Potiphar "took him and had him thrown into the prison where the king's prisoners were confined." That is a hard turn for Joseph. I think this one hurts, friends.

The answer is that he grants him favor with the warden. Verse 21 says the LORD "extended kindness to him, granting him favor in the eyes of the prison warden." The LORD is still with him, even in a prison. It's the warden's eyes where the favor lands.

The answer is that the warden puts all the prisoners in his care. Verse 22 says, "And the warden put all the prisoners under Joseph's care, so that he was responsible for all that was done in the prison." All of them, friends. Joseph is behind those walls, and he's still given responsibility.

The answer is False. The warden is hands off. Genesis 39:23 says, "The warden did not concern himself with anything under Joseph's care, because the LORD was with Joseph and gave him success in whatever he did." Any boss would love to hand things off like that. The text gives the reason: the LORD was with Joseph.
